P1_fx_receipts.question: Can resident individuals receive foreign currency for services or digital exports? Any conversion or repatriation rule?
P1_fx_receipts.answer: Yes. The State Bank of Pakistan's Foreign Exchange Manual (Chapter 12, as updated) defines freelancers as all resident individuals providing digital/online services paid from abroad, lets banks process their export proceeds on a self-declaration basis when no contract exists, and lets them keep USD 5,000 per month or 50% of proceeds (whichever is higher) in a foreign-currency export account (ESFCA). The rest is credited in PKR. Retained balances can be converted to PKR any time, but no foreign-currency cash withdrawal is allowed inside Pakistan.

It is superseded by EPD Circular Letter 17/2023. Do not cite it as current.

P2_fcy_account.question: Can individuals hold a foreign-currency bank account?
P2_fcy_account.answer: Freelancers: yes. Banks must open an Exporters' Special Foreign Currency Account (ESFCA) at the same time as the freelancer's primary PKR account. Balances can pay for personal and work-related current-account items (digital services, marketing, subscriptions, certifications, study) without SBP approval, can be converted to PKR any time, and cannot be withdrawn as foreign-currency cash inside Pakistan. General foreign-currency accounts for residents who are not freelancers were not researched under this item.

L1_registration.question: Must an individual selling digital products or services register a business? How (sole proprietor), cost, online?
L1_registration.answer: No separate business registration is required. SMEDA (a government SME agency) says a sole proprietorship needs no prior registration with any government department. The practical registration is with the tax authority (FBR): an individual e-enrolls online with CNIC, phone, email and address, adding a business name and address if they have business income. SMEDA's booklet says FBR is the registering authority for sole proprietors and that applying for an NTN has no official cost; that booklet's other figures date from 2018-19. Companies register with SECP, which is optional and only needed for a company. Punjab residents can also register a sole proprietorship on the Punjab Business Registration Portal, which links to FBR. Freelancers who want the 0.25% export tax rate register with PSEB (see L7), and PSEB requires a personal NTN with no business name.

L2_tax_id.question: Tax identification number requirement and how to get it
L2_tax_id.answer: The tax ID is the NTN (National Tax Number). For individuals, the 13-digit CNIC number itself is used as the NTN. It is obtained by online e-enrollment with FBR (Iris), which issues the NTN/registration number and a password. Being registered and filing returns also matters for the export-income regime in L3, because section 154A's final-tax treatment requires that a return has been filed.

L3_income_tax_foreign.question: How residents' foreign-sourced or digital income is taxed
L3_income_tax_foreign.answer: Residents are taxed on both Pakistan-source and foreign-source income. For export receipts there is a special regime (Income Tax Ordinance s.154A, text amended up to 30 June 2026). The bank deducts tax when the foreign-exchange proceeds are realised: 0.25% of proceeds for computer software, IT or IT-enabled services exports by persons registered with PSEB (tax years 2024 up to 2029), and 1% for other export of services ('any other case'). The deduction is a FINAL tax on that income if the return is filed, withholding statements are filed if required, and sales tax returns are filed if required. PSEB-registered IT exporters are exempt from the sales-tax-return condition. No foreign tax credit is allowed. FBR's Budget 2026-27 salient features confirm the 0.25% rate was extended to Tax Year 2029.

L4_vat_gst.question: VAT/GST rate, registration threshold, treatment of exported services and digital services
L4_vat_gst.answer: Pakistan splits sales tax. Goods fall under the federal Sales Tax Act 1990: standard rate 18%, and exported goods are zero-rated. Finance Act 2026's sales-tax amendments do not change section 3, so the 18% stands. People selling digitally ordered goods within Pakistan through a marketplace, website or app must register (cottage industry excepted). Services are taxed by the provinces (Sindh SRB, Punjab PRA, KP KPRA, Balochistan BRA) and by the federal government for Islamabad. Sindh, verified: standard rate 15%, and IT consulting, IT design and development, and software licensing services exported and delivered outside Pakistan are exempt if paid in foreign exchange through banking channels into the exporter's business bank account and reported to SBP. Punjab, KP, Balochistan and Islamabad rules were NOT verified (see notes).

L5_data_protection.question: Data-protection law: name, year, in force?, regulator
L5_data_protection.answer: No comprehensive personal data protection law is in force. The Ministry of IT & Telecom's Data Governance Policy (June 2026) lists the 'Personal Data Protection Law' as anticipated and says the policy will be updated when it is enacted. A May 2026 secondary guide says the Personal Data Protection Bill was approved by the Federal Cabinet but has not passed both houses of Parliament. Current relevant statutes named by MoITT include the Prevention of Electronic Crimes Act 2016 (PECA) and the Electronic Transactions Ordinance 2002. Since there is no PDP regulator yet, sellers serving foreign customers should expect the customers' own laws (e.g. GDPR) to matter more.

L6_consumer_ecommerce.question: E-commerce / consumer-protection law relevant to online sales
L6_consumer_ecommerce.answer: Electronic contracts and signatures are legally recognised under the Electronic Transactions Ordinance 2002, which extends to the whole of Pakistan. Consumer protection is mostly provincial; the federal one is the Islamabad Consumers Protection Act 1995, listed on Pakistan Code. Provincial acts were not fetched. Domestic online sales also carry tax rules. Income Tax Ordinance s.6A taxes payments for digitally ordered goods or services delivered from within Pakistan through locally operated platforms or websites: 1% when paid digitally via a payment intermediary, 2% for cash on delivery via courier. Export proceeds taxed under s.154/154A are excluded. Sellers of digitally ordered goods must register for sales tax (see L4). The Ministry of Commerce's e-Commerce Policy 2.0 (2025-30) exists only as a stakeholder draft and couldn't be fetched.

L7_incentives.question: Government incentives or schemes for IT/digital exporters or freelancers
L7_incentives.answer: 1) The PSEB freelancer registration unlocks the reduced 0.25% final export tax instead of 1% (L3) and exempts PSEB IT exporters from the sales-tax-return condition for final-tax treatment. It costs Rs 1,000 per year to register and Rs 2,000 per year to renew. It needs a personal NTN with no business name, CNIC and a personal bank account letter, and is open to individuals. The certificate is issued 2-5 working days after payment is verified. Renewal needs an export revenue summary and an income tax return. 2) Under SBP, freelancers can keep USD 5,000 per month or 50% of export proceeds (whichever is higher) in an ESFCA foreign-currency account and spend it without approval (see P1/P2). 3) Sindh exempts exported IT services from provincial sales tax, subject to conditions (L4).

W1_workarounds.question: Simple, legal routes around payment barriers for a beginner (no misrepresentation, nominees or sanctions evasion)
W1_workarounds.answer: Barriers: Stripe does not accept merchants here; PayPal is not available. Simple legal routes: (1) Sell digital products or software through a merchant of record: Paddle (software/SaaS only; each seller reviewed), Lemon Squeezy (bank payouts), Polar. The platform is the legal seller to your customers, handles card payments and consumer VAT/sales tax, and pays you out. You still declare the payouts as your income at home (see L3). (2) Sell services on Upwork, which is available here (not on its restricted list). Which withdrawal methods you get (bank, PayPal, Payoneer, etc.) depends on the country and shows in your account. (3) Creator income through the YouTube Partner Program (available here). (4) Paid apps and in-app sales through Google Play (merchant registration available here). (5) For direct clients, a bank transfer (SWIFT) into your own local account always works. Follow the local foreign-exchange rules (see P1) and keep invoices. (6) Local official channel: The State Bank of Pakistan lets freelancers receive export proceeds on self-declaration when there is no contract. Banks must open an Exporters' Special Foreign Currency Account (ESFCA) alongside your PKR account. Payoneer offers an 'Individual' account type (P1/P2/P5). Avoid: opening accounts with a foreign address, a relative's or friend's identity, or a VPN to look like you are elsewhere. It breaches platform terms (accounts and funds get frozen) and can break anti-money-laundering or sanctions law.
